checks: The average stays jointly continuous in direction and position, nonnegative and convex in physical coordinates. The single affine ceiling is continuous in the unit direction, majorizes each measured support and touches the common source. A common finite field supremum gives the same homothet bound for every probability.

Weak compactness on compact metric Θ and the common modulus of continuity imply uniform convergence of the averaged fields along a subsequence. At a regular old point the tight-cut gap is nonnegative and O(ε), so positive radial loss can accumulate only at its unique supporting normal and a fixed-ceiling contact.

The contact normal supplies the lower radial bound. A tight normal at each positive-loss endpoint gives the upper bound after discarding its nonnegative old gap and dividing by a radial support distance tending to a positive number. At a noncontact a positive-loss subsequence would contradict the contact limit.

The radial shell Jacobian and uniform bound justify dominated convergence after dividing the losses by ε. Supporting full, supporting empty, proper traces, pure-base equalities and the d=1 endpoint-counting case have the stated selectors. Finiteness gives uniformity over the menu. Source 4c4db2dc9830c76a §§3–4 (7)–(13) uses the same fields and contact indicator.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use a singleton cut index with ceiling h_p(u)+A(u)·(z-p). Actuality and completeness give the same compatible canonical family. Each averaged field satisfies the nonnegative continuous convex hypotheses, and the common supremum gives the same homothet bound and shell formula.

overlap.comparison: Its fixed-action radial and cap derivatives include the selector and homothet arguments. The draft adds uniform errors for all probability averages of a compact field family, with the field average taken before the cut.
This realizes finite nonnegative speed combinations using product-index cuts. It does not control the error uniformly over probability averages on a compact parameter space.

readability: The statement and proof specify the necessary hypotheses and quantities.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The compact common-ceiling family yields an actual averaged-field cut, with a pointwise radial speed linear in the probability and a first-order error uniform in the probability for any fixed finite closed-cap menu.
